=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/claude_pool_health_alert.sh:lines around the new truncation block (last_run_diff added the 3700-char cut and the 3900-char backstop) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The marker `… (truncated: the alert is longer than 3700 characters; see the run log)` is added after the 3700-character substring, and `text="${text:0:3900}"` then cuts again at 3900, so the "longer than 3700 characters" wording does not match the final 3900 bound.
  WHY: This is cosmetic, only a wording inconsistency, not a functional defect.
- scripts/claude_pool_health_alert.sh and scripts/claude_pool_daily_usage.sh:`health_args+=("--chatgpt-status=${CHATGPT_POOL_STATUS}" …)` (health_alert) and `report_args+=("--chatgpt-status=${CHATGPT_POOL_STATUS:-}" …)` (daily_usage) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The ChatGPT status JSON is passed as a single argv element, so a low `ARG_MAX` or an oversized broker payload would make `execve` fail and the call would fall back to invalid_probes / "probe results unreadable".
  WHY: A broken or oversized ChatGPT status would silently kill the Claude alert/report; the engine caps accounts at 64 and fullmatches names, so the realistic blast radius is low, but the shell has no such check.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===

- HARDENING_SUGGESTION: scripts/claude_pool_health_alert.sh (line ~88: `health_args+=("--chatgpt-status=${CHATGPT_POOL_STATUS}" ...)`) and scripts/claude_pool_daily_usage.sh (lines ~105-108)
  PROBLEM: The raw ChatGPT status JSON is passed as one argv element. If the payload goes over Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN (128 KiB), running claude_engine.py fails and the script falls into the invalid_probes / "probe results unreadable" path, which suppresses the Claude output too.
  WHY: The suggested fix is to guard the argument, e.g. `[ ${#CHATGPT_POOL_STATUS} -le 100000 ] || unset CHATGPT_POOL_STATUS`, so an oversized payload becomes "no ChatGPT data" (estimated 4-6 lines changed); HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.

It attributes the failures to the test environment (no PyYAML, non-executable /tmp, no jq). It found every Phase 4 deliverable present and the last-run changes correct.
